overview.overview:
Indiana has moved further from the national average in each of the last two presidential cycles, backing Republican candidates by about 16 points in 2020 and 19 points in 2024. The forecast expects a Republican win of roughly 13 points, a somewhat narrower margin than 2024 because the national environment is expected to shift modestly toward Democrats.

Even so, Indiana remains well to the right of the nation as a whole, and its 11 electoral votes are not considered competitive. The plausible range of outcomes spans from a narrow single-digit Republican win to a blowout exceeding 20 points, with essentially no realistic path for Democrats to carry the state.
overview.watch: A much larger national swing toward Democrats than current conditions suggest would be needed to bring Indiana's margin into single digits.
key_factors: Indiana's consistent Republican lean of roughly 18 points relative to the nation
A national environment expected to shift a few points toward Democrats, trimming but not erasing the Republican margin
The absence of any state-specific polling or candidate home-state advantages to alter the baseline
